source_refs.note: Topic 1.4.3 with the cost example (PDF 17-19, printed 14-16). The printed contingency and total do not follow from the items; the QA line omits '2'; the answer key's (c) for MCQ 9 contradicts the text. Recorded.

blocks.text: Estimating the cost of a software project is a critical step in planning and management. It means predicting the total expenses needed to complete the project; an accurate estimate helps with budgeting, allocating resources and setting realistic expectations.

items: Development team: the number of developers, their expertise and hourly rates; specialists may charge more.
Technology stack: the technology, languages and tools chosen; some need more resources or specialist knowledge.
Project duration: longer projects usually cost more.
Risk management: plans for possible risks add cost; a contingency fund covers unforeseen issues.
Quality assurance: testing, bug fixing and meeting quality standards.

blocks.text: Example: a company in Pakistan wants a 6-month (24-week) online shopping app with user registration, product listings, shopping cart, payment integration and order tracking, built with React Native, Node.js and MongoDB by 1 project manager, 2 frontend developers, 2 backend developers, 1 UI/UX designer and 2 QA testers, with a 10% contingency fund.

The total covers all parts of development, from planning and design to implementation and testing, and shows how each factor adds to the cost. The book prints the contingency as PKR 1,604,000 and the total as PKR 19,644,000; ten per cent of the PKR 18,040,000 subtotal is PKR 1,804,000, which makes the total PKR 19,844,000. You do not need to know programming to start a software project: you can post your idea on freelancing platforms where developers bid on it, and seek investors to fund it (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Which factor does not influence a software cost estimate (MCQ 8)? What is a contingency fund for (MCQ 9)?
blocks.explanation: The number of meetings held, option (c). A contingency fund covers unexpected costs, option (a), such as scope changes or integration problems; the book's answer key gives (c) for MCQ 9, which does not match the text.

items: Cost estimation predicts total expenses for budgeting, resources and expectations; factors: team, technology stack, duration, risk (contingency), quality assurance.
Example: subtotal PKR 18,040,000, 10% contingency 1,804,000, total 19,844,000 (printed 1,604,000 and 19,644,000).
